newsitem.title: USA: Florida says P&O line misleads passengers.
newsitem.headline: Florida says P&O line misleads passengers.

text.p: Florida on Tuesday charged in a civil complaint that Princess Cruises, a unit of Peninsular & Oriental Steam Navigation Co. of Britain, was deceiving passengers on fees.

The filing in Broward County Court here seeks $15,000 for each violation of a state consumer law and follows an agreement in February in which Carnival Corp. and other leading cruise ship companies agreed to include most so-called port fees in advertised prices.

The fees, sometimes covering operating expenses, added as much as $150 to advertised ticket prices and were often described as government-imposed fees, according to Florida Attorney General Bob Butterworth.
Only a small amounts went to government agencies, Butterworth said.
"By keeping portions of these add-on fees for itself, Princess was able to advertise lower cruise prices than would otherwise be possible," Butterworth said in a news release.
Princess said in a statement that the charges had no merit and that Florida had never detailed any violation committed by Princess.
"We believe that our advertising in the state of Florida has always communicated to consumers the full price of the cruise ...," the company said.
Butterworth said he filed the complaint against Princess after the cruise line refused to abide by the agreed restrictions negotiated with Florida, the most popular place for cruise lines.
